name: Demio
tagline: Run a small live webinar on self-managed video and collect registrations

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1 host; 50-attendee room; 3-hour sessions; 4 people on stage; 15 event admins
tiers.notes: The supplied snapshot said $59/month; the live Starter rate is $63 monthly or $45/month annually.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: 150, 500, 1,000 or 3,000-attendee rooms; 8-hour sessions; 6 people on stage; 25 event admins
tiers.notes: Price changes dynamically by room size and billing period; current dollar values were not exposed in page text.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 150, 500, 1,000 or 3,000-attendee rooms; 10-hour sessions; 10 people on stage; 50 event admins
tiers.notes: Official page displayed $196/host/month paid yearly, but did not expose which attendee-room selection produced it.

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.limits: Custom hosts, room size, service and contract terms
tiers.notes: Referenced in the current pricing FAQ; public price is not disclosed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day Growth trial is capped at 20 attendees and 1-hour sessions and includes HubSpot integration
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (30% lower); Premium and Unlimited plan changes require 30 days' notice
pricing.hiddenCosts: Concurrent sessions require multiple paid host seats; Zapier setup services cost $150, concierge onboarding is paid, and the Boost add-on auto-converts after its 14-day trial at an undisclosed price.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Demio, run a small live webinar on self-managed video and collect registrations. The hard boundary is webinar media infrastructure, registration, engagement, replay hosting, analytics, and support, plus real-time media infrastructure and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Run a small live webinar on self-managed video, collect registrations, issue signed room links, and keep recordings only when every participant is clearly informed.
whatYouLose: webinar media infrastructure, registration, engagement, replay hosting, analytics, and support
ongoingBurden: TURN capacity, codecs, browsers, packet loss, scaling, recording, consent, abuse, monitoring, and incident response
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Demio because video products survive because real-time media quality and global reliability are infrastructure businesses, not weekend interface projects. The recurring cost buys TURN capacity, codecs, browsers, packet loss, scaling, recording, consent, abuse, monitoring, and incident response, not just the visible interface.

rejectedAlternatives.name: BigBlueButton
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Good live room, wrong product: registration pages and replay marketing are still your job.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Jitsi Meet
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A meeting room is not a webinar funnel; registrations, reminders and replay pages are absent.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a small private meeting service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Demio in an empty repository.
Use Docker Compose, Jitsi Meet, a small Next.js 15 control panel, PostgreSQL, and TURN; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: run a small live webinar on self-managed video, collect registrations, issue signed room links, and keep recordings only when every participant is clearly informed.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Deploy Jitsi Meet through pinned Docker images and configure a dedicated TURN service.
Build an owner panel for rooms, signed invitations, expiry, lobby mode, and participant limits.
Show connection diagnostics for camera, microphone, browser, bandwidth, and TURN reachability.
Make recording disabled by default and require an on-screen consent state for every participant.
Store room metadata and audit events, but do not store media unless explicitly enabled.
Add health checks, bandwidth dashboards, backup, restore, upgrade, and incident instructions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a global media edge network.
Deliberately leave out public webinar scale and telephony.
Deliberately leave out regulated recording, enterprise compliance, and guaranteed support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
